newsitem.title: INDIA: Speculative bidding helps India shares record gains.
newsitem.headline: Speculative bidding helps India shares record gains.

text.p: Hectic bidding by speculators in blue-chip stocks on increased hopes of positive government announcements helped Indian shares climb to higher levels on Wednesday, dealers said.
Firm market sentiment drove up key pivotals. "It's a headline-driven market," said chief dealer Sanjeev Choithani at Pashupati Advani,a local firm.

Foreign funds, a major influence in Indian markets, have yet to resume buying in a big way after seasonal holidays, but local institutions and speculators have been active bidders in stocks in the last few weeks.

Players are now banking on policy measures to boost the markets. The policies which are likely to be announced by the government in mid-January are expected to give a fillip to industrial growth and revive dull capital markets.

"The market is waiting with a lot of expectations," Neeraj Batra, president at Hinduja Finance, an investment firm, told Reuters. "The best part of the recent rally is that foreign funds have not been active players...to some extent, small investors are coming back to the market."
"The return of small investors is needed if a rally has to be sustained," Hinduja's Batra said.
Indian industry is expected to do better in the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) than in the first, the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) said in a recent report.
While there were indications of a slowdown in the industrial sector, there were no signs of a recession, the Bombay-based independent research group said.

SBI was up 2.25 rupees to 250.0, Bajaj Auto 11.0 to 917.75, MTNL 3.25 to 231.0. TISCO lost 3.50 to 186.25 and Reliance 0.75 to 218.25. The Cazenove Indian GDR index added 1.65 points, or 2.17 percent to 77.82 on Wednesday.
